title: E1024 document store split across rwb-document, rwb-case and the shared decision-record topic
source: RWB-E1-024; Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 42; DP-01, DP-03, DP-06, DP-07
description: The legacy story stores a document, reads the case through the in-process CaseDirectory, writes the decision log in the same transaction and emits the local DocumentStored event. In the target the document and the document index are rwb_document (P5), the case is read through the P3 contract, the parameters and the reference data come from the P3 contracts and the decision record leaves on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 owned by rwb-decision. The Ownership Map publishes no P5 operation that returns the case or party link with the document, and P7 is not in the integration dependency list of this slice.
evidence: RWB-E1-024 sections 4, 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slides 16 (P5 contract) and 42 (DocumentStored, DecisionRecorded); Ownership Map P3 case, P5 document, P7 decision-log; WP B-ITG-W1-04 I list
proposed: The suite asserts the stored document through the P5 contract, the case through the P3 contract and the party key through the P1 customer contract; the decision record is read on rwb.decision-record.v1 and the central ledger is proved in RWB-ITG-E1027-ITG.

title: E1025 document-type load path and field dictionary after the reference-data ruling
source: RWB-E1-025; Architecture v5 slides 15, 16 and 41; DP-01, DP-07
description: The legacy story loads the DOCUMENT_TYPE table through the P4 POST /admin/reference-loads endpoint and reads LOV-RETENTION through the P4 list service. In the target the reference data and the LOV are owned by P3 rwb-case (DP-07) while the document type rows are P5's own table and P5 implements the loader; the WP lists P1 and P5 only, so the P4/P3 load path and the approval separation of duty are outside the slice and no P1 field-dictionary path is named in the story.
evidence: RWB-E1-025 sections 3, 4 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 15 (P3 reference data) and 16 (P5 contract); Ownership Map P3 reference data and P5 document_type; DP-07
proposed: The suite reads the document type version in force through the P5 contract and the P1 field dictionary through the P1 contract; the load and the approval are proved in the P3 reference-data and P5 APP stories, and the separation of duty stays a data rule.

title: E1026 attach and search screen as a gateway-bff composite over P5 and P3
source: RWB-E1-026; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 20; DP-06, DP-07, DP-19
description: The legacy screen calls the P5 document endpoints and the case record view directly. In the target SCR-30 is a gateway-bff composite route over the P5 document endpoints and the P3 parameter and reference-data contracts, and the malware scan and the checklist source behind the upload path are not named in the Ownership Map; the composite path and its aggregation shape are not published.
evidence: RWB-E1-026 sections 4, 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slide 16 (P5 contract), slide 20 (screens through gateway-bff); Ownership Map P3 parameters and P5 documents; DP-19
proposed: The suite asserts the composite response through gateway-bff against the P5 list and the P3 parameter contracts, and the upload path through the P5 contract; the scan is asserted only through its result on the store call.

title: E1027 decision codes and reference data move to P3 while the writer and the ledger are PLT and P7
source: RWB-E1-027; Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 42; Temporal and Drools design slides 11, 14 and 28; DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-17
description: The legacy writer reads LOV-DECISION through the P4 list service and the rwb.decision.code.* parameters from the shared catalog. In the target the writer is the platform decision-record library (PLT), the central ledger is rwb_decision (P7), the parameters are P3's and the LOV is P3's reference data; the WP lists PLT and P7 only. The legacy data-lake copy of the decision log (RWB-E1-014) is retired (DP-17) and has no target path.
evidence: RWB-E1-027 sections 3, 4, 11 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 14 (P7 contract), 27 and 42 (DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1); Temporal and Drools design slides 11, 14 and 28; DP-17
proposed: The suite drives the PLT decision-record library through its conformance caller and asserts the record in the P7 central ledger and on rwb.decision-record.v1; the decision codes are asserted as values in force, not read from a P3 store, and no lake copy is asserted.

title: E1028 durable timers replace JOB-05 and the P1 account-date path leaves the slice
source: RWB-E1-028; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slides 13 and 24; ASM-A6-tables-12; DP-05, DP-10
description: The legacy story runs JOB-05 on Quartz every five minutes and reads the account dates and the holiday calendar through the P1 published interface. In the target the clock is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow, JOB-05 and TimerDue are retired, the timer row stays a P3 projection behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers and TimerBreached stays on rwb.case.events.v1; the WP lists P3, P4 and P7 only, so the P1 account-date and holiday path is outside the slice and the exact Temporal timer visibility surface is not published. The deviation events come from rwb-deviation (S8, wave 2), so the wave 1 pause is triggered through the P3 case action contract.
evidence: RWB-E1-028 sections 3, 4 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 42 (TimerDue retired, TimerBreached P3) and 44 (JOB-05 retired); Temporal and Drools design slides 13 and 24; ASM-A6-tables-12; Ownership Map P3 timers and S8 wave 2
proposed: The suite asserts the timer through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers, the breach on rwb.case.events.v1 and the decision record in P7, and it proves the catch-up by pausing the worker; the P1 account-date and holiday inputs are proved in RWB-P3-E1028-APP, the deviation pause goes through the P3 case action at wave 1 and no TimerDue is asserted.
